name: Spear Sergeants
headerMeta: Heroic era · Melee Infantry / Shields · 215 leadership · Honour Tree · Mastery available
pitch: A low-cost shield-wall anchor that toggles Cover Commander to stack a debuff on whatever hits it next, holding lines in PvE and early progression more than it wins competitive TW. Good players now hunt it with lifesaver doctrine, and house Q&A rates it behind ISG for that reason.

doctrines.note: 100 melee dmg taken → bleed, +15% dmg/move while bleeding

doctrines.note: alt build: DMG taken / full block

veterancy.label: Bottom line
veterancy.body: Adds an actual brace/stun-on-hit mechanic and is generally better against cavalry — though cav matchups matter less now since the unit has fallen behind as an anti-cav pick.

veterancy.label: Top line
veterancy.body: Favors players who lean more on Cover Commander mode.

battleRole.positioning: In Cover Commander, stand at the edge of the unit's cluster rather than the middle — models in the middle can get flanked from behind as the formation wraps around a target. {6} Don't push in hard until you've stacked the −10%-per-hit penetration debuff (up to −50% at 5 stacks) on what's about to hit you. {1}
battleRole.formation: Line and Block: shield wall highly resistant to ranged damage, even from high-tier ranged units, despite visual gaps in the line. {6} Sheltron (tight circle): generally a poor PvP choice for shield units — the tight radius fits under siege AoE templates (musket bombs, trebuchets, scorpion bolts) — though this unit benefits from it somewhat more than comparable shield units, and it's strong in PvE (AI loops around the circle while models keep stabbing, including turning inward). {6} Advance holds the current formation while moving — in sheltron the models keep the circle shape and stab inward; in line they hold on approach but break on contact (unlike Stalwarts, which keep pushing through). {6} Formation-lock note: models keep fighting whoever engaged them and won't reposition mid-fight — switching to any other formation immediately forces a break-and-reposition. {6}
battleRole.tips: Stay on Cover Commander, toggling it off and back on every 2 seconds to refresh the buff granted at activation. {1} While in Cover Commander: damage taken drops 60% immediately, decaying to 40% over time; damage dealt rises 45%, decaying to 30%; the decay rate is 6 seconds. {1} In live PvP, actively swap between shield-wall and Cover Commander rather than locking into one for a whole engagement — e.g. hold a capture point in shield wall, flick to Cover Commander to screen from cavalry threatening from behind. {6} An apparent stagger/stun proc on hit has been observed even without a brace node slotted — flagged as an undocumented quirk, not a confirmed mechanic. {6}

cards.name: ISG

cards.name: Azaps
cards.why: Azaps guides name Spear Sergeants (with Imperial Spears, pike militia) as the reason to run piercing defense over blunt

cards.name: Cavalry (general)
cards.why: full-mastery Spear Sergeants are "surprisingly effective vs cavalry charges, if used correctly" — brace/stun + Awareness Doctrine mitigate charges, though this has faded as an anti-cav pick over time

cards.name: Ranged units / pikemen
cards.why: line-formation shield wall blocks incoming fire; Advance is best used to close the distance on ranged units or heavy frontal-damage dealers like pikemen

controls.notes: Cover Commander: toggle off/on every 2s to refresh the buff — damage taken 60%→40% and damage dealt +45%→+30%, both decaying over 6s. {1} Per-hit penetration debuff: −10%, stacking to −50% at 5 stacks — don't commit until it's stacked on the target. {1} Advance: holds formation while moving; in sheltron the unit keeps its circle and stabs inward, in line it holds until contact then breaks. {6}

gaps: The Amya OP has no Counters/Loses-to/Struggles-vs section at all — this is an absence in the source, not an unfilled placeholder; matchup coverage above leans on incidental mentions from other units' guides and one disputed house claim.
House Q&A's ISG-over-Spear-Sergeants claim was directly disputed in-thread by another house member ("isg also self heal") and never walked back — recorded as an open disagreement, not resolved.

StaRBuRsT's 2025-09-22 attack-meta farm list places Spear Sergeants in its era/tier row but is marked likely-stale (pre-dates the 2026-06-22 patch cutoff) and adds no build detail beyond that placement, so it isn't cited as a claim.
Amya's doctrine/build guidance was last edited 2026-05-26, pre-dating the 2026-06-25 Chaos patch — may be stale for the current season, with no post-patch update visible.
KnightStalker's undocumented stagger/stun proc (no brace node slotted) is presented as a surprising discovery, not a confirmed mechanic — unverified against current patch notes.
